docs.text: Not so fast, Governor. Lake Michigan was named after the Ojibwa word mishigami, which means "great water" or "large lake." Native peoples get deference.

The lake received its current name from the French, who named it for the Huron (Wendat) people. Their maps call it Lac des Hurons, meaning Lake of the Hurons. The Ojibwe called it Giigoonh-zaaga'igan, meaning Lake of Fishes, due to the bountiful fish in the lake. 🧵 5/6

lake michigan is a translation of the ojibwe word “mishigami” = large lake or great water. at one point it was named “lake of stinking water” because of the algae bloom stank & the french attempted to call it lac du illinois but ultimately mishigami —> lake michigan is what stuck.

The Ojibwe name for Lake Michigan is “Michigami” meaning “really large body of water”. #puremichigan #lakemichiganbeach

The word mishigami is an Ojibwe word that means "large water.” It is the origin of the name of the state of Michigan and Lake Michigan. So if we’re renaming bodies of wate, I suggest the Mishagami Sea.

The name "Michigan" comes from the Ojibwe word mishigami, which means "big lake" or "great water.” The name Illinois comes from the Miami-Illinois word irenweewa, which means "he speaks in the regular way". Come visit Lake Michigan any time, Gov.
Au contraire. Lake Michigan was named after the Ojibwa word mishigami, meaning "great water" or "large lake."

Fun fact, some people argue that Michigan is named after the Ojibwe word mishigami meaning large water or large lake. So Lake Michigan is Lake Large Lake. Side note, i said lake too much and it looks weird.
